REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - JANUARY 26, 2026 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact City of Cerritos ADA/504 Coordinator, Drew Schneider, at (562) 916-1314 at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to public meetings.

The California Court of Appeal has concluded that sectarian prayer as part of the City Council meetings is not permitted under the Constitution.

Agenda Report

Public Comments and Suggestions
This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Verbal comments may be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Mayor/Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Mayor/Chair extends.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the legislative body, there will be no separate discussion of these items. If a legislative body member requests separate consideration, the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition,
verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

If the City Council adjourns to Closed Session, the City Council/Successor Agency will reconvene into Open Session after its conclusion and designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY,
JANUARY 26, 2026, 7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Bishop Robert Magalogo, Church of Jesus Christ of
  Latter-Day Saints.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cub Scout Pack 529.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Mike Taylor (City Employee Retirement).

REORDERING OF THE AGENDA
At this juncture, the City Council, by consensus, reordered the agenda to consider Public
Hearing Item 8A prior to consideration of Item 5B.

5B.  Review and consideration of the Mayor’s nominations for appointments to internal
  ad hoc working groups and external boards, commissions, and committees
  (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, consideration of this item was continued to a
  future City Council meeting.

  There were no public comments received on this item and no action was taken.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Al Barlevy expressed support for the City’s continued conduct of the annual Dr.
  Martin Luther King, Jr. Day Ceremony.

  David Pylman spoke regarding public meeting conduct and projected completion of
  the Del Amo Boulevard Bridge Replacement and Signal Enhancements project.

  Raymond Kim spoke regarding voter efforts and recent recall election proceedings in
  other California local agencies.

  Rocky Pavone spoke regarding his previous and future campaigns in City elections.

  Kurtis Forsythe expressed concern regarding his recent interactions and meetings
  with City officials and Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department personnel.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern regarding City finances, and rates and assessments
  paid by Cerritos residents.

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk announced that at the meeting, one (1) written comment
  was submitted for Item 6, for inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies of
  the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made during regular
  business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

  ADOPTING UPDATED WATER AND SEWER RATES WHICH SUPERSEDE THE EXISTING

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING A LOW-INCOME WATER AND
  SEWER UTILITY ASSISTANCE PROGRAM AND PROVIDING A FIXED BIMONTHLY
  DISCOUNT OF $40 FOR ELIGIBLE RESIDENTIAL CUSTOMERS (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Alvin Papa, Director of Public Works/City Engineer. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 10

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the proposed water and sewer rate
  adjustments:

  Rocky Pavone  Benjamin Ao  Carmelita Tiongson
  Carol Chen  Case van der Linden  George Vara
  Charlie Joslin  Lew Gentiluomo  Raymond Kim
  Mel Cortez  Jabed Zaman  Terence Wu
  Amanda Teneyck  Steve Patel  Chung Fu Luan
  Robert Shavelle  Steve Henderson  Kirit Chauhan
  Merri Wheaton  Denny McCartney  Steven Stallings
  Teresa Gutierrez  Zenas Tham  Richard Kith
  John Kitos  Sam Desai  Kyo Kim
  Judy Chiu  Daisy Lagasca  Timothy P. Golden
  Carla McKirnie  Carla Gilhuys  Richard Chung
  Samuel Pedace  Leah Nass

  The following individuals expressed support for the proposed water and sewer rate
  adjustments:

  Deborah Berry
  Al Barlevy

  Salem Garawi inquired regarding the potential future of the City’s water quality if the
  utility increases are not approved; the phasing out of the City’s General Fund support
  to the subject budget accounts; and regarding the Proposition 218 protest form
  tabulation and potential validation process.

  Maggie Villa expressed concern regarding the conduct of City public meetings and
  freedom of speech at meetings/public hearings.

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting, the City Council
  received full-text, unredacted copies of the sixteen (16) written comments submitted
  for Item 8A, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official
  record. Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can
  be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period and
  public hearing closed at 10:04 p.m.

  The Mayor announced that no additional written protests may be submitted,
  however, if any were in line to submit a form prior to the close of the public hearing,
  those forms would be accepted by City Clerk staff.

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, upon cursory review of the written protest forms, reported
  that 6,400 protest forms were received, that the number was manifestly less than
  one-half of the eligible parcels (Total parcels: 15,148 water; 14,998 sewer), and
  there was an absence of a majority protest.

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to schedule a report at a future

  revenue sources such as and including a possible Utility User Tax; Transactions and

  decreases to water and sewer bills.

  MOTION (DIED DUE TO LACK OF A SECOND): It was moved by Hong, to direct the
  City Manager to work with the City’s Finance Division to research alternate revenue
  sources aimed at reducing proposed water and sewer rate adjustments, including
  identifying immediate funding opportunities for Capital Improvement Projects and
  additional revenue sources. The motion died due to lack of a second (COUNCIL).

  ORIGINAL MOTION (SUPERSEDED BY SUBSEQUENT, RECONSIDERED
  MOTION): It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Pulido, to:

  WATER AND SEWER UTILITY ASSISTANCE PROGRAM AND PROVIDING A
  FIXED BIMONTHLY DISCOUNT OF $40 FOR ELIGIBLE RESIDENTIAL

  3. Authorize a budget amendment in the amount of $200,000 from the General Fund to
  implement the Low-Income Water and Sewer Utility Assistance Program for the
  remainder of the 2025-2026 fiscal year (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Pulido, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Hong, Tse
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  The motion and vote above were superseded due to a timely and valid motion for
  reconsideration taken later in the meeting, and then subsequent motion and vote on the
  original question. These actions, though taken at a later junction of this meeting, are

  the majority on the original motion. To be considered timely, the motion to reconsider
  must be made at the meeting where the item was first voted upon. The matter may be
  discussed and debated as if it were on the floor for the first time. If no new motion is put
  forth, it would stand as if action on the matter under consideration never occurred.
